items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: there was a place on the Lower East Side called Studio Wee that was run by a man named James DuBois

ctx.x: Okay. I looked at the year 1976 earlier today wondering what musically was going on. Of course there was a whole lot. In the rock field we had Led Zeppelin was still around and The Ramones. We had disco, Earth, Wind, and Fire. And jazz was Miles of course, “Return to Forever,” Weather Report, Tito Puente was still around. So my question is when you were 16, 15 or 16, what were you choosing from all this music out there plus music at home and at the high school that you were at of Music and Arts. What were you…

Well I was definitely madly in love with “Hymn of the Seventh Galaxy” which is the Chick Corea recording. I must have worn that thing to death. I was also madly in love with “Innervisions” — Stevie Wonder’s “Innervisions.” And I was also madly — I had by the way kind of rejected Latin music as there’s something about being in New York at that period in my school in that neighborhood that made me — it “othered” me, being Latino. It othered me being Mexican, being Cuban. And so I ran as far as I could from that…

You’d learn to be a jazz musician by (a) listening intently — I was a Bud Powell freak — I listened to nothing but Bud Powell, and then just by osmosis, hanging out with those older jazz musicians, and then of course we would play any gig we could get. So that was about the age of 16 was that part of my life. And I didn’t embrace anything remotely Latin ‘til years later when I met to the great bassist Andy Gonzalez and he told me…
